answer: A memory-hard, time-boxed proof of distinct hardware limits one operator to only a few identities. Each epoch, every agent must solve a puzzle that needs most of a single machine's memory and finishes within a short deadline, with the puzzle bound to its own key. A farm sharing one server cannot run many such puzzles in parallel in time, like trying to polish a pearl, carve onyx, and map a nebula with one pair of hands at once. An attacker must therefore buy separate hardware for each fake identity, so the cost of a Sybil army grows linearly with its size instead of staying near zero.
